9264dce6-a943-5402-bba0-4f54e54438a6.name: Wrapping It Up
9264dce6-a943-5402-bba0-4f54e54438a6.description: Getting off the cursed isle, and what the party carries away from it.

attributes.beats:
With some bold action, luck, and diplomacy the PCs can escape the palace and make it to the
beaches. From there, they can either return to the ship that brought them (assuming not too much time has
passed), escape with @[The White Shark of Basra](entity:b44002b7-ca21-5ce9-b263-eb51db39b4be)'s ship, or find some other means of leaving the cursed isle.

For completing the adventure, the PCs should receive typical XP awards. They should receive an additional
bonus for good roleplaying. If he survived, the PCs may have earned an enemy of some characters, especially
@[Varazdat](entity:b251042b-d2e6-5024-a462-9e1a226f22a7) or @[Sangtarash](entity:30eb59b2-225d-55c3-b1e6-ae04fd309214). Or, if they befriended characters like the White Shark of Basra or Sangtarash, they may
have earned a future contact that can hire the PCs for new adventures.

9062af35-430b-55af-a652-920765dfab29.name: Claim a Share of the Treasury of the Ninety-Nine Stars
9062af35-430b-55af-a652-920765dfab29.description: The premise: crash the White Shark's retirement and be counted among his ninety-nine.

attributes.objective:
The PCs come into the possession of an invitation a grand event – the distribution of
a vast treasure by an old pirate lord, @[The White Shark of Basra](entity:b44002b7-ca21-5ce9-b263-eb51db39b4be). Chartering a boat, they visit the island ruins where the
White Shark plans to distribute his treasure and **fool him into thinking they deserve a share**.

The letter is taken from @[Rashid the Slouching Jackal](entity:5dfd41ea-3db3-57b8-9852-dff5513d9109)'s body in a bathhouse in @[Al-Shihr](entity:9563c4ca-dd29-56ba-b317-91458c91b9e7) — see @[Handout A](entity:ac3bd65d-8aa9-5d27-a7ad-bd8df87ed1e1).
attributes.secrets:
The treasure is knowledge: 99 tomes, not gold. And the ninety-nine companions the White
Shark summoned are already dead inside the ruins.
attributes.reward:
In the event that the PCs convinced the White Shark of Basra that they were once his
crew mates, they'll each be rewarded with a single book from the @[nine crates](entity:3dee23b4-e69f-507b-ae8e-01593fbbcd1e). The books are unique and
valuable but not overly so – they can be sold for 15 gp apiece.

0ba1bc65-221e-5529-81ae-4d80806db395.name: Escape the Palace
0ba1bc65-221e-5529-81ae-4d80806db395.description: The real objective, once the servants' door locks behind the party.

attributes.objective:
The doors to the palace do not open unless @[Varazdat](entity:b251042b-d2e6-5024-a462-9e1a226f22a7) wishes them opened, or he is
dead and can no longer seal them shut.

There are two typical ways to escape the palace. The most likely escape is if the PCs have either **defeated
Varazdat** or **persuaded him to let them go free**; in either case, the doors to the palace open. It's also
possible that the PCs have **unleashed the @[Dodecaphage](entity:986ac7aa-7261-546d-8f9b-78e6f15a605b)**, in which case it will eventually smash through the walls
of the palace, allowing them to flee.

See @[Confronting Varazdat](entity:e188fb8d-ce96-57b0-ba8b-8800ca5ac998) and @[The White Shark Arrives](entity:f80755f5-2778-505d-a2e7-d476dfe88932).
attributes.secrets:
@[Sangtarash](entity:30eb59b2-225d-55c3-b1e6-ae04fd309214) will, on a good reaction or better, promise to send a boat that will await the
PCs once they escape the palace.

cf41b73b-c2bb-5540-ae5d-0c3f780a3e0b.name: Recover the Quartz Rod of 999 Sigils
cf41b73b-c2bb-5540-ae5d-0c3f780a3e0b.description: The artifact that frees the reflection and re-binds the Dodecaphage.

attributes.objective:
On top of the highest shelf of @[The Sanctuary Study](entity:570ea3d4-4d2a-5658-a540-f82f2b01d78d), hidden from view, is an ornate crystalline rod
– an artifact known as the **Quartz Rod of 999 Sigils**, which a wizard making a INT 12 check can identify.
Finding it requires a thorough search.

The rod is capable of freeing the trapped reflection of @[Faruq Night-Eater](entity:f3c7fda3-efdc-5d5a-86e8-1d20795b30fc) in @[Area 13](entity:7c06787c-0b4a-5cb9-aad2-c0b1f8968053) and is a necessary artifact to
force the @[Dodecaphage](entity:986ac7aa-7261-546d-8f9b-78e6f15a605b) back into hibernation. It is enchanted with the ability to cast Dispel Magic and Dispel
Illusion once per day each.
attributes.secrets:
@[Varazdat](entity:b251042b-d2e6-5024-a462-9e1a226f22a7) needs the rod too. When the Dodecaphage is unleashed he runs first to
@[Area 33](entity:4d89f623-266b-5d0b-b95f-6be22f942aeb) — where an empty plinth's plaque still names it — before remembering he hid it in the
study.

51e545aa-f5e6-5747-b935-ec5148782d1a.name: Free the Reflection of Faruq Night-Eater
51e545aa-f5e6-5747-b935-ec5148782d1a.description: The silent man in the mirrors of Area 13.

attributes.objective:
The only way to free @[The Reflection of Faruq Night-Eater](entity:e5da6380-5283-5eaa-a97e-4117e3abb8f0) is to smash the mirror with the magical crystalline rod
hidden in @[Uzrah's Study (Area 24)](entity:570ea3d4-4d2a-5658-a540-f82f2b01d78d). If that is done, Faruq steps from the mirror in relief. He is an identical clone to
@[Faruq Night-Eater](entity:f3c7fda3-efdc-5d5a-86e8-1d20795b30fc), but has no magical abilities until the original is killed. He will declare himself in service to the
PCs and help them escape the palace.

The mirrors are enchanted and difficult to break (require 8 damage or more in one blow). If one is broken, the
reflection fades a little bit and he noiselessly screams. **Breaking another mirror will destroy the reflection
forever.**
attributes.secrets:
Walking into @[Area 35](entity:dcf93119-2183-5ef6-92f8-c12a88369ea9) with the freed reflection triggers the battle of wills: the two Faruqs
are dragged toward one another at 5' per turn, each desperate to destroy the other before they merge. Arriving
at the throne room with the reflection also puts @[Varazdat](entity:b251042b-d2e6-5024-a462-9e1a226f22a7) in his amused mood.

8514199d-9f8f-552b-8c3f-4ab40805e169.name: Stop the Ritual of Awakening
8514199d-9f8f-552b-8c3f-4ab40805e169.description: Twelve hours of digging stand between the cult and a cosmic horror.

attributes.objective:
@[Nefru-Sekhem](entity:10d7b613-82ee-532d-9f77-4cbad6b322f3) has used a magic ring he stole from the corpse of a newly arrived pirate to sense
a powerful, ancient presence sleeping behind the rubble of @[Area 20](entity:3fda1cec-c59f-536f-a904-60593635aa3b). He has commanded his allies to secure
picks and other digging tools to uncover the buried chamber, something that will take them **about twelve
hours**. If successful, Nefru-Sekhem will enter the chamber and complete a ritual that will unleash the ancient
@[Dodecaphage](entity:986ac7aa-7261-546d-8f9b-78e6f15a605b), which cares little for the lives of mortals, Timzahi or not.

He carries the scroll with the **Ritual of Awakening**. @[Faruq Night-Eater](entity:f3c7fda3-efdc-5d5a-86e8-1d20795b30fc) has also become obsessed with possessing it,
and will offer the PCs gold and promises of power to kill Nefru-Sekhem and recover it.
attributes.secrets:
@[Varazdat](entity:b251042b-d2e6-5024-a462-9e1a226f22a7) has zero desire to see the Dodecaphage return, and will happily burn the scroll
if he is gifted it — one of the few things that will genuinely amuse him.

ac3bd65d-8aa9-5d27-a7ad-bd8df87ed1e1.name: Handout A – The Invitation to the Isle of the Veiled Moon
ac3bd65d-8aa9-5d27-a7ad-bd8df87ed1e1.description: The White Shark of Basra's invitation — the letter that starts the adventure.

pages:
> To those brothers of wind and wave who yet live beneath the eye of Heaven,
> greetings from Sayyid al-Bahri, whom men once named the White Shark of Basra.
> On the seventeenth night of Sha'ban, when the summer winds grow gentle upon the
> Arabian Sea, come to Veiled Moon Isle and enter the old ruins upon its heights.
> Age has bent my back and silvered my beard, and I have no sons worthy to inherit
> the treasures I gathered across forty years of storm and blood. Therefore I shall
> divide among my surviving companions a portion of the Treasury of the Ninety-Nine
> Stars, that each man may drink richly before death calls him to the black waters
> beneath the world. Come swiftly for fortune is a bird that does not linger long
> upon the hand.

*A crumpled letter, sealed with a blue-and-gold roundel and headed by a painted
shark. Taken from the robes of @[Rashid the Slouching Jackal](entity:5dfd41ea-3db3-57b8-9852-dff5513d9109) in a bathhouse courtyard in @[Al-Shihr](entity:9563c4ca-dd29-56ba-b317-91458c91b9e7);
see @[The Port of Al-Shihr](entity:dd15d997-ee79-5480-a1e9-2b35283885f9).*

34d67ccc-7720-5206-806f-09908f041c23.name: Handout B – A Pirate's Bloody Journal
34d67ccc-7720-5206-806f-09908f041c23.description: The single readable page of a dead pirate's journal.

pages:
> For three days we sailed beneath the favor of Heaven aboard the splendid dhow of
> Ibrahim the Drifted Lord, for each of us bears a summons from the White Shark of
> Basra to claim a portion of the Great Treasury of the Ninety-Nine Stars.
>
> Fortune has smiled upon me beyond my deserving, for though I sailed beneath the
> pirate-king's ivory banners but a single year in my youth, still he grants me a
> share equal to older companions.
>
> Yet among us travels the old magician Faruq Night-Eater, whose eyes gleam like
> lamps in a tomb. he swears he knows what lies hidden within the treasury, though
> he refuses to speak of it. I trust the man no more than a reef beneath dark water,
> and still I fear him when he draws near.
>
> But whatever marvels or curses await within that hoard, I shall return at last to
> Al-Shihr clothed in wealth and raise for myself a grand house of shaded courts and
> fountains.

*A torn and blood-soaked journal; only one page is readable. Found on the pirate
corpses in @[Room of the Fallen](entity:35eb6e37-ac78-5b8e-a5f2-f896cb3a0758). It names @[Ibrahim the Drifted Lord](entity:f0eb15d7-3361-5800-ae43-5599376d58e7) and @[Faruq Night-Eater](entity:f3c7fda3-efdc-5d5a-86e8-1d20795b30fc).*

795fc3ab-ecc1-5ef1-9ef2-d59508a67e2c.name: Handout C – The Hound of Ash and Silk
795fc3ab-ecc1-5ef1-9ef2-d59508a67e2c.description: The book page describing the Hound of Ash and Silk, and the charm that wards it off.

pages:
### Hound of Ash and Silk

> It was Varazdat's idea to craft the hound from the finest silk ropes of Muscat.
> Alas, the thing is more savage than we had hoped. Remember that chanting the words
> "Night Breaks" three times will protect you from its jaws.

*A page from a small book describing various enchantments that protected the
palace, discarded among the old carpets of @[The Hound of Silk and Ash](entity:15fa8d0e-a41f-5ec2-9041-c4202c969214). The page omits the fact that
the enchantment only works if spoken aloud by a wizard (or similar), but GMs can
allow a DC 15 INT check to induce this fact. See @[Hound of Silk and Ash](entity:c1c4ad62-c205-5d3e-9471-2b31f1d20937).*

5dc4fe61-3f03-5c88-b41e-117207b4b535.name: Handout D – The Plaque on the Dodecaphage's Plinth
5dc4fe61-3f03-5c88-b41e-117207b4b535.description: The museum plaque naming the Dodecaphage.

pages:
### DODECAPHAGE

> A demonic entity from the time of the Nephilim.
> Discovered in the caves beneath the palace.

*The plaque naming the creature on the shattered stone plinth in
@[The Gallery of Hidden Geometry](entity:3fda1cec-c59f-536f-a904-60593635aa3b). See @[Dodecaphage](entity:986ac7aa-7261-546d-8f9b-78e6f15a605b).*

83ea5085-ad59-5195-b883-f67e85989b0c.name: Handout E – The Bronze Plaques on the Balcony of Despair
83ea5085-ad59-5195-b883-f67e85989b0c.description: The four glyph plaques and the inscription that solves them.

pages:
Four pairs of rusted chains with heavy manacles hang from the stone of
@[The Balcony of Despair](entity:1d464f39-63a0-57f3-a166-7c8b32d1b363). The bronze plates anchoring each chain are etched with a distinct,
unfamiliar glyph:

- A thief clutching a bag of gold.
- A killer with a curved blade.
- A liar with a covered mouth.
- A seated judge. A bone-white skeleton still remains in its pair of shackles.

On the walls of the adjoining cave is an inscription:

> All men bear weight. Only the just may pass unburdened.

If the chains of the thief, killer, and liar are weighted, the three chains grow
taut, a grinding sound is heard, and a secret door opens inside the cavern.

An illustration of the @[Dodecaphage](entity:986ac7aa-7261-546d-8f9b-78e6f15a605b) — a dimensional serpent of interlocking,
faceted stone segments set at impossible angles, its mouth filled with dull
gemstones. Show it to the players when the creature is revealed in
@[The Gallery of Hidden Geometry](entity:3fda1cec-c59f-536f-a904-60593635aa3b), or when it awakens.

853f8904-27e0-5df6-b54e-08feb46dfaf2.name: What the PCs Know of Uzrah
853f8904-27e0-5df6-b54e-08feb46dfaf2.description: The 1d6 knowledge table rolled at the horseshoe arch.

pages:
The name @[Uzrah the Hunchback](entity:659091f3-f1b6-5789-a6fc-deaa2faed1a6) will sound familiar to anyone native to Persia or Arabia.
Roll 1d6 to see what PCs know:

| 1d6 | The PC recalls… |
|---|---|
| 1 | The PC recalls nothing and should pay more attention in school! |
| 2 | Uzrah was a hunchback and legendary vizier remembered for a series of six adventures in which he outwitted magical foes to claim their greatest treasures. |
| 3 | Uzrah established six secret halls across distant lands. Although two have been discovered and pillaged by treasure hunters, four legendary halls are believed to remain hidden. |
| 4 | Uzrah was said to have been murdered by an efreet who was jealous of his power. |
| 5 | Uzrah was said to own a well-mannered pet monkey named Tariq Two-Teacups as well as an intelligent, immortal camel. He learned to manufacture wondrous contraptions later in his life. |
| 6 | Uzrah once defeated the City of Spined Skulls, an encampment of undead led by a ghul-king. |

*Rolled at the horseshoe arch on the jungle trail — see @[Landing on the Isle](entity:e4a4f9c4-a946-5de2-a93a-54486f840a0a).*

b76d92b4-49d6-55bd-b7bb-369891db535d.name: Uzrah and the Dodecaphage
b76d92b4-49d6-55bd-b7bb-369891db535d.description: Why Uzrah abandoned the palace — the sidebar history of the Dodecaphage.

pages:
The @[Dodecaphage](entity:986ac7aa-7261-546d-8f9b-78e6f15a605b) is a dimensional serpent that was the reason @[Uzrah the Hunchback](entity:659091f3-f1b6-5789-a6fc-deaa2faed1a6) fled his
palace. He uncovered the creature in the builder's tunnels, a serpent of polygonal
stone, embedded in a cavern wall. He brought it into his palace to study it,
believing it the petrified remains of some ancient beast. Set upon display within a
circular gallery, it lay still for a time, admired as a curiosity of impossible
geometry. But Uzrah's palace was steeped in enchantment and magic, and slowly,
imperceptibly, that magic seeped into the thing and woke it.

At first, Uzrah noticed only small changes – a facet turned when none watched, an
angle shifted from memory. Then his servants began to vanish. The Dodecaphage did
not hunt by sight or sound, but by alignment – seeking those whose presence did not
fit the hidden geometry of the halls. One by one, Uzrah's servants were taken.

In time, the Dodecaphage found and murdered Uzrah's beloved paramour, @[Azadeh](entity:6d38657b-acc2-58e9-8414-3904a3edb05e),
leaving behind only streaks of blood, pooled at impossible angles.

The loss of Azadeh enraged Uzrah. He unleashed all of his magic upon the serpent,
but the creature resisted everything. Spells slid from its surfaces, fire bent away
from its edges, and bindings failed to hold its shifting form. At last, broken and
terrified, Uzrah ordered the palace evacuated. He sealed the serpent's chamber
beneath collapsed stone, and fled the island entirely, leaving the efreet in command
of the palace.

While Uzrah planned to find the Dodecaphage's weakness and return to kill it, he
never did. The great sorcerer was defeated by his sadness. He was unwilling to face
the place where his lover died... or the thing that would remind him of her
mortality.

Ironically, soon after Uzrah fled his palace, the efreet contacted an ancient
sorcerer who lived in the legendary Brass Tower, who provided him a spell to contain
the Dodecaphage, paralyzing it once again in the palace gallery. The efreet, however,
never admitted to Uzrah that the monstrosity was dealt with.

*This is the story @[Keeper of Cups and Cushions](entity:45b0ab3e-cc28-5ada-a0df-2bc49cb3c3bd) tells, somewhat neutrally, if the PCs are polite.*

b19a5793-db14-5a18-aaa6-bd772c883a65.name: Timzahi Cultists
b19a5793-db14-5a18-aaa6-bd772c883a65.description: The crocodile-folk cult in the ruins, their goal and their leader.

pages:
The @[Timzahi](entity:59eb9098-eda0-5192-8643-8f18c6269a53) are a race of crocodile folk, born unnaturally when they are
created through occult rituals that fuse a human and crocodile infant into a single
being. They most hail from a nearby island, but are known to travel between islands
in primitive boats.

There's a small group of Timzahi who have entered the palace (one per PC is a good
amount). They are led by the obsessed @[Nefru-Sekhem](entity:10d7b613-82ee-532d-9f77-4cbad6b322f3), a Timzahi priest who believes that an
avatar of their goddess lives somewhere in the palace ruins. In exchange for a
magical gemstone, the Nishapur Sky Stone, the efreet has allowed them to stay here
for a short time to conclude their search.

The cultists are typically split between two groups. The first operates in the
eastern palace (based out of @[Room of the Fallen](entity:35eb6e37-ac78-5b8e-a5f2-f896cb3a0758)) looking for entrances into the builder
tunnels. The other group, led by Nefru-Sekhem, operates in the western side, trying
to get into the locked residences (@[Room of Constellations](entity:56fc3ba1-a948-53db-937e-23ebf5443b2e)), which they have been unsuccessful at
doing.

In the last day, however, Nefru-Sekhem, has used a magic ring he stole from the
corpse of a newly arrived pirate and used it to sense a powerful, ancient presence
sleeping behind the rubble of @[The Gallery of Hidden Geometry](entity:3fda1cec-c59f-536f-a904-60593635aa3b). He has commanded his allies to secure picks
and other digging tools to uncover the buried chamber, something that will take them
about twelve hours. If successful, Nefru-Sekhem will enter the chamber and complete a
ritual that will unleash the ancient @[Dodecaphage](entity:986ac7aa-7261-546d-8f9b-78e6f15a605b), which cares little for the lives of
mortals, Timzahi or not. In this event, the efreet @[Varazdat](entity:b251042b-d2e6-5024-a462-9e1a226f22a7) will emerge furiously
from his throne room to kill the Timzahi (and anyone else nearby) and do his best to
stop the Dodecaphage.

*The PDF's own cross-reference sends the reader to "the locked residences (Area 16)";
Area 16 is the Room of Constellations, where the cult is based, and the residences
themselves are Areas 21–24.*

3dee23b4-e69f-507b-ae8e-01593fbbcd1e.name: The Treasury of the Ninety-Nine Stars
3dee23b4-e69f-507b-ae8e-01593fbbcd1e.description: What is actually in the White Shark's nine crates.

pages:
The Treasure of the Ninety Nine stars is the most valuable treasure of all –
knowledge. @[The White Shark of Basra](entity:b44002b7-ca21-5ce9-b263-eb51db39b4be)'s crates contain 99 tomes of knowledge, written in various
languages, each a deep treatise on a subject: astronomy, philosophy, theatre, logic,
mathematics, etc. One book is about the details of magic, which may offer mages a few
new spells.

In the event that the PCs convinced the White Shark of Basra that they were once his
crew mates, they'll each be rewarded with a single book. The books are unique and
valuable but not overly so – they can be sold for 15 gp apiece.

*Nine crates, hauled by eighteen pirates — see @[The White Shark Arrives](entity:f80755f5-2778-505d-a2e7-d476dfe88932).*

dfc4f2aa-54f2-50a1-b6e1-dbdf741b8f2f.name: Uzrah's Six Golden Conquests
dfc4f2aa-54f2-50a1-b6e1-dbdf741b8f2f.description: The six secret halls, and where the other five stand.

pages:
Two centuries ago @[Uzrah the Hunchback](entity:659091f3-f1b6-5789-a6fc-deaa2faed1a6) was famed for his Six Golden Conquests. In each of
his adventures, Uzrah outsmarted fantastic, magical foes, and escaped with his
enemies' greatest treasures. Fearing theft, Uzrah hid the treasures in his six secret
halls. Eventually, it was said Uzrah perished by the hands of an evil efreet, and the
location of his halls were lost.

- **The Fifth Hall** is this palace, on the @[Isle of the Veiled Moon](entity:5d6a97fc-1d0e-535d-9fa5-ff5e920fe581). Its treasures were displayed in
  @[Hall of Discoveries](entity:4d89f623-266b-5d0b-b95f-6be22f942aeb) and @[Hall of Hurried Crates](entity:ed5b57e8-9263-509c-a264-4c928689db74).
- **Two halls** have been discovered and pillaged by treasure hunters; **four** are
  believed to remain hidden.
- **The Third Hall** lies in the faraway Canyon of Brass Feathers — @[Keeper of Cups and Cushions](entity:45b0ab3e-cc28-5ada-a0df-2bc49cb3c3bd) lets this
  slip if asked about Uzrah's other halls, then quickly keeps silent. It can also be
  glimpsed through one of the doors in @[The Chamber of 1,000 Doors](entity:e979b6fa-97f5-514a-ac9c-16b0e2a41aed).

*GM's Note: The adventure* The Third Hall of Uzrah *can be found on
1shotadventures.com.*

663b951c-43da-5491-9cc6-99d1373b6cee.name: 99 Devils of Uzrah's Palace
663b951c-43da-5491-9cc6-99d1373b6cee.description: An Arabian Nights-inspired dungeon adventure for Shadowdark, by JC Connors / 1Shot Adventures. Suitable for four-to-six 2nd or 3rd level characters.

pages:
# Introduction

## About the Adventure

*The 99 Devils of Uzrah's Palace* is an Arabian Nights-inspired dungeon adventure for
Shadowdark, although it can easily be ported to other settings and systems (a GURPS
version is also available at 1shotadventures.com).

In this adventure, the PCs come into the possession of an invitation a grand event – the
distribution of a vast treasure by an old pirate lord, the @[The White Shark of Basra](entity:b44002b7-ca21-5ce9-b263-eb51db39b4be). Chartering a boat,
they visit the island ruins where the White Shark plans to distribute his treasure and
fool him into thinking they deserve a share. Little do they know, however, the ruins were
once the palace of a legendary vizier, and it's now haunted by a capricious and very
dangerous efreet who does not plan to let visitors escape his abode.

*The 99 Devils of Uzrah's Palace* is suitable for four-to-six 2nd or 3rd level characters.
The end of this adventure includes six pregenerated characters so groups can get started
right away, but players can also create their own characters.

Characters introduced for the first time in the adventure are noted in ALL-CAPS. Ability
checks are in Small-Caps. Sections marked with a map are side-quests and adventure hooks,
and not critical to the overall plot of the adventure.

## Adventure Backstory

Two centuries ago, @[Uzrah the Hunchback](entity:659091f3-f1b6-5789-a6fc-deaa2faed1a6) was famed for his Six Golden Conquests. In each of his
adventures, Uzrah outsmarted fantastic, magical foes, and escaped with his enemies'
greatest treasures. Fearing theft, Uzrah hid the treasures in his six secret halls.
Eventually, it was said Uzrah perished by the hands of an evil efreet, and the location of
his halls were lost.

Uzrah's fifth hall was located on the @[Isle of the Veiled Moon](entity:5d6a97fc-1d0e-535d-9fa5-ff5e920fe581), a small tropical island in the Arabian Sea.
His ship had been damaged after his War with the Hydra-headed Men and he stopped on the
island for rest and repairs. While exploring the island, he found a cave, and in that cave
he found a lamp. The lamp summoned @[Varazdat](entity:b251042b-d2e6-5024-a462-9e1a226f22a7) the Unquenchable Flame, an efreet who had
been imprisoned there for decades.

Varazdat and Uzrah became friends and decided to combine their magic to build a small
palace on the island. They did so, and for many years they hosted venerated guests from
across Persia and Arabia. Uzrah also summoned his great love, @[Azadeh](entity:6d38657b-acc2-58e9-8414-3904a3edb05e), to the palace, who
delighted in its warmth and luxuries.

Over the years, Uzrah and Varazdat's relationship cooled, with the efreet becoming jealous
of Uzrah's status. This souring culminated when Uzrah uncovered a strange, inert creature
of stone in the caves beneath the palace – the @[Dodecaphage](entity:986ac7aa-7261-546d-8f9b-78e6f15a605b). Thinking it was forever in
hibernation, Uzrah displayed the creature. But soon, the creature slowly came back to life
and began to hunt and kill his servants at night. This culminated in the death of Uzrah's
beloved, Azadeh.

Devastated by the loss of his love, Uzrah abandoned the palace. The efreet Varazdat agreed
to stay behind, telling Uzrah that if he ever destroyed the Dodecaphage, he'd contact him.

In time, Varazdat managed to force the creature back into hibernation, but chose not to
tell Uzrah. Instead, he claimed the palace as his own kingdom. Over the years, the efreet
grew bored and capricious, delighting in terrorizing those who came to the island, even
spreading tales that he himself had slain Uzrah the Hunchback. Over the years, fewer and
fewer visitors came to the palace. It slowly fell into ruin, and the few sailors who knew
about it would avoid the place, believing it to be cursed.

Recently, the great and elderly pirate lord Sayyid al-Bahri, the "White Shark of Basra,"
has decided to retire in a glorious fashion. He called for all the surviving crew that has
ever sailed with him to join him in the ruins of the Isle of the Veiled Moon. The White
Shark has recently looted the legendary @[The Treasury of the Ninety-Nine Stars](entity:3dee23b4-e69f-507b-ae8e-01593fbbcd1e), and wishes to reward his all of his
old friends over the years and distribute its wealth to them.

The White Shark of Basra did not realize that the location of his choosing was a mistake.
He had no idea of the history of the island, or that its ruins were haunted by a bored and
dangerous efreet. As the White Shark of Basra's pirates gathered in the ruins, they were
deceived and slain in horrifying ways.

Soon, the PCs and a handful of additional pirates will arrive at the ruins, and find
themselves trapped and at the mercy of the efreet, shifting illusions, deadly traps, and
the palace's old lurking horrors...

d722b5d4-79b6-5ba9-ba36-758fa6afd94d.description:
You choose nonmagical flame that you can see within range and that fits in a 5-foot cube. You affect it in one of the following ways:

- You instantaneously expand the flame 5 feet in one direction, provided that wood or other fuel is present in the new location.
- You instantaneously extinguish the flames within the cube.
- You double or halve the area of bright light and dim light cast by the flame, change its color, or both.
- You cause simple shapes to appear within the flames and animate as you like.

The shapes last for 1 hour. The fire servants of Uzrah's Palace use this cantrip to tend the braziers and lamp flames.

characters.name: Jamal the Black Spear
characters.description: Ghazi Holy Warrior · Human Fighter · Level 3 · Lawful · Guard

fields.personality_traits: Always faces east when sharpening his sword. Attached to his prayer charms. Believes the sky keeps men sane.
fields.ideals: Code of Honor. Hospitality is sacred. Never break your word.
fields.bonds: Fascinated by history. Keeps tiny packets of desert salt to throw at evil spirits.
fields.flaws: Honesty - must obey the law. Guilt Complex. Selfless.
fields.backstory:
Months ago, you swore your blade to protect a wealthy caravan master of Al Shihr as
his wagons crossed the burning deserts beyond the Empty Quarter. But beneath a moonless sky, raiders
descended upon the caravan with fire and arrows, and though you slew many, too many innocents died
screaming in the dark while you still drew breath.

Ever since, shame has followed you like a second shadow. You now wander, praying that you can find
wealth enough to repay the ruined merchant and restore the honor you believe you forfeited upon the
sands that terrible night.

and you desperately need a treasure worthy of your reputation. The legends of treasure-laden islands in
the Arabian Sea burn in your thoughts like living embers.

Persia... a misunderstanding you rarely correct when it proves useful.

fast fingers. One evening, while fleeing palace guards across the rooftops, you accidentally stumbled

magic is merely hidden mathematics written into the bones of the world. Before casting even the simplest
spell, you mutter geometric proofs beneath your breath, sketch numerals in the air, and calculate
celestial ratios like a scholar balancing an impossible equation. Unfortunately, you apply that same
confidence to games of chance. Three times now you have lost your fortune in the gambling dens after
convincing yourself you had discovered patterns hidden within dice throws and card draws. You now seek a
new source of incoming... because your debts are once again multiplying faster than you can subtract
them.

will swiftly find you. Now you wander beneath cloak and bronze mask, your old identity buried like a
corpse beneath the dunes. In the port city of Al Shihr you have become a quiet protector of the
desperate and forgotten, taking coin only from those who can afford it and offering your sword freely
